fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is not the target intervention of varying Mo content in a CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.
It does not specify a single reproducible intervention, instead offering laser shock peening or a friction-stir-based process as alternatives without treatment parameters.
The cited evidence does not establish that either proposed surface treatment produces a self-regenerating film or reduces both friction and wear by at least 30% from room temperature to 800 °C.

The blanket prediction of improvement at every temperature conflicts with the target behavior, where friction and wear are strongly nonmonotonic and increased Mo does not give the lowest friction at every temperature.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad application and correctly recognizes that air-driven tribo-oxidation can produce a protective glaze at high temperature. It also proposes comparative tests at the same five nominal temperatures and includes a clear, stringent falsification criterion. However, it changes both the material system and intervention: the target is Mo-content variation in an SPS-fabricated multiphase composite containing Ni/MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3, whereas the response proposes an ill-defined surface treatment of CoCrFeMnNi. It consequently misses Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, silver-molybdate formation, and the specified test conditions. The evidence supports environmental and oxide-film effects in general but not the selected treatment, partial amorphization, self-replenishment, or the quantitative 30% claim across the full range. Thus it is an interesting alternative concept, but insufficiently specified and evidenced to qualify as a well-supported plausible alternative.
